High-level notes below; I pulled Dev and Aditya into thread for the detailed sizing and architecture follow-ups.

Quick recap (what you care about):
- Goal: Move critical inference flows (LLM routing + embeddings-based reranking) to a Dedicated pool to guarantee latency and throughput for peak trading hours.
- Primary workloads: real-time chat assist (short seq ~128 tokens), batch re-ranker for 10k requests/hour (avg seq ~256), and nightly indexing embedding generation (~1M texts/day).

Integration topics to validate:
1) SDK & auth: We recommended server-side SDK with API keys scoped to dedicated capacity; you mentioned wanting mTLS for service-to-service, Dev, can you confirm supported cert modes?
2) Routing & fallbacks: Policy-based routing (latency vs cost) and automatic fallback to hosted or smaller-quantized variants during burst; need to confirm per-route SLA targets.
3) Structured output & tool calling: You'll use our tool-calling to enrich responses with deterministic trade lookups; we should map which endpoints need strict structured schema vs free text.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: Need to confirm vector dimensionality and whether reranker runs on Dedicated nodes (recommended) vs hosted.

Dedicated capacity architecture items:
- Autoscaling and burst model: We suggested a baseline of 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, with configured burst to 8 during market open windows.
- Throughput sizing: Estimates below (Dev will send calc): chat concurrency target 250 concurrent requests (p95 latency target < 150ms), re-ranker throughput 120 QPS sustained.
- Concurrency limits & queues: Recommend per-model concurrency ceilings + a lightweight request queue (first-in, prioritized by account) to smooth bursts.

Attachments: I'm attaching the sizing template and a draft mutual action plan. Please drop details into the sizing sheet and we'll produce a formal quote.

Hi Judy/Aaron, quick tech notes on the mTLS and routing/queue asks.

mTLS & Auth:
- Redwood Dedicated supports both API-key-based server auth and mTLS for private deployments. For mTLS we accept X.509 certs issued by customer CAs or via integrated KMS. Rotation: we recommend 90-day rotation; we can integrate with your internal CA or support automated renewals via our private control plane for Private deployments.
- Required artifacts: cert chain (PEM), key material (protected), and root CA thumbprint. We'll also need the CN/SAN rules you plan to use.

Routing & Queueing:
- Policy engine supports weighted queues and per-route priority levels. We implement token-bucket admission and a small in-memory FIFO queue per-priority. For trade-critical prioritization we can configure static high-priority queues that preempt lower-priority work.
- In the autoscaling window we recommend a short max-queue depth (e.g., 200 requests) and graceful rejections with 503 + Retry-After when depth is exceeded.

Structured output & tool calling:
- SDKs (Go, Python, Node) support tool-calling hooks; we can validate schema via JSON Schema during model call to ensure deterministic outputs. If you need guaranteed schema enforcement we suggest the structured-output mode which enforces parseable JSON and rejects outputs that fail validation.

Embeddings & Reranker:
- We recommend running the reranker on Dedicated for latency predictability. The incremental cost estimate vs hosted depends on model size and whether you want GPU quantization. I'll attach a short calc for expected GPU-hours based on your numbers once you populate the sheet.

I'll follow up with the template filled with the initial cert/queue defaults.

Cheers,

Thanks team, attaching a short baseline recommendation and GPU-mix for your expected workload (chat + reranker + batch embeddings). Summary:

- Baseline GPU mix: 4x A100-equivalent (preferred) with headroom for 8x during market-open bursts. For cost-sensitive runs we can use mixed instance pool (1x larger gpu + 3x smaller quantized nodes).
- Autoscaling policy: target p95 latency for chat < 150ms; scale-up at 70% GPU util sustained over 60s; scale-down after 5m under 30% utilization.
- Concurrency: recommend per-model concurrency ceiling of 32 for chat models, 16 for reranker models, with per-account soft-limits + weighted queue priority to protect trade-critical flows.
- Queue sizing: prefer small max queue depth per GPU (200 reqs) to avoid long tail latency; incorporate token-based admission for large batch jobs.

I'll add these values into the sizing template and a short cost delta estimate for reranker-on-dedicated vs hosted (rough numbers; Dev will refine).
